[LEXP.6.1] Two built-ins specific to `Json`-typed slots (see [LGRA]):

| Function | Meaning | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `len(<Json>)` | array length at runtime | `Int` |
| `has(<Json path>)` | whether the path resolves | `Bool` |

idris.name: lexp_6_1__has
idris.note: `has(<Json path>)`: whether the path resolves, a Bool for every document ([LNUL.8.4]'s one absence test). A root that is not a document -- a `null` root included -- is a trap here, as both runtimes raise a type mismatch; no well-formed program reaches it, since `has` is a builtin that demands a value of a particular kind and an unnarrowed `Json?` receiver is [LNUL.5.1]'s compile error, `DS_VALIDATE_NULLABLE_UNNARROWED` (compiler/LNUL.5.1_has_on_unnarrowed_json_refused, and its narrowed twin compiles).

idris.name: lexp_6_1__len
idris.note: `len(<Json>)`: the array's length, an Int; of anything else [LEXP.6.2]'s TypeError, a trap here.

idris.name: lexp_6_2__len_is_an_arrays_alone
idris.note: The table's `Int` row: an Int for every array, and nothing else answers.

idris.name: lnul_8_4__has_separates_the_missings
idris.note: The table's `Bool` row: `has` answers a Bool for every path and document, true of a present JSON null and false of an unresolved path, which the read alone cannot tell apart.
